name: statistikat/STATcubeR
what_it_holds: R interface to Austria's STATcube REST API and data.statistik.gv.at (Statistics Austria's open-data portal), found via the sdmx topic cluster.
why_useful: Austria isn't in our explicit gap list but is a Eurostat-reporting EU tourism market (Vienna short-term-rental regulation is already tracked); this gives a programmatic route to Austrian accommodation-statistics tables if the regional model is extended.
themes: European tourism statistics tooling: Eurostat tour_occ / tour_ce clients, INE Spain Frontur Egatur EOAT tourist-apartment tables, ISTAT, INSEE, Destatis, ONS travel, Portugal INE
why_all: Austria isn't in our explicit gap list but is a Eurostat-reporting EU tourism market (Vienna short-term-rental regulation is already tracked); this gives a programmatic route to Austrian accommodation-statistics tables if the regional model is extended.

name: Monthly-Amtrak-Ridership-Forecasting
what_it_holds: Committed monthly Amtrak system-wide ridership series, Jan 1991 - May 2013 (the classic Hyndman/forecasting-textbook Amtrak series), used for R time-series forecasting (ARIMA/exp smoothing). ~269 monthly obs.
why_useful: Long back-history (22+ years) of a national ground-travel demand series; useful only as a macro travel-demand backdrop / seasonality reference for gap #10 (rail/road capacity), not point-in-time and stops in 2013 so not current.
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: Long back-history (22+ years) of a national ground-travel demand series; useful only as a macro travel-demand backdrop / seasonality reference for gap #10 (rail/road capacity), not point-in-time and stops in 2013 so not current.

name: AMTRAK-Ridership-Forecasting
what_it_holds: Same classic 1991-2013 monthly Amtrak ridership dataset as jimmy-nguyen-data-science's repo, re-hosted for a separate forecasting exercise.
why_useful: Duplicate of the above; only worth a one-line note since identical series appears in multiple student repos (confirms it's a stable, easy-to-find historical series).
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: Duplicate of the above; only worth a one-line note since identical series appears in multiple student repos (confirms it's a stable, easy-to-find historical series).

name: Amtrak_Ridership_Crawl
what_it_holds: Selenium crawler that scrapes Amtrak's own site for annual ridership by individual station (station-level annual counts, not a national monthly aggregate).
why_useful: A working method to get station-level Amtrak ridership (finer grain than the national monthly series above); could be adapted to pull current-year station data for a ground-travel cross-check, though it is a scraper of Amtrak.com and would need to be re-run rather than used as-is (no committed data, last updated 2020).
time_coverage: annual, vintage unclear (crawl-time dependent), repo from 2020
size_hint: scraper only, no committed data file
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi

name: amtrak-gtfs-rt
what_it_holds: A GTFS-Realtime feed generator/parser for Amtrak (live train positions/schedule adherence), actively updated (Apr 2026). No historical ridership counts -- this is train-position/frequency data, not passenger counts.
why_useful: Could be used to build a service-frequency/capacity proxy for Amtrak corridors going forward (gap #10 capacity angle), but has no historical archive and does not measure ridership or dollars -- weak fit for the ABNB nights/ADR forecast.
